text: Vomiting once is usually minor: monitor and offer small amounts of water. Two or more episodes in a day means contact the vet, and postpone stressful activities such as grooming or rough play. Four or more episodes, or vomiting with lethargy or blood, is urgent and needs a vet now.

A single loose stool is usually minor: monitor. Three or more episodes in a day means contact the vet and postpone stressful activities such as grooming. Six or more episodes, or blood in the stool, is urgent.
Unusual tiredness may mean pain or illness. Reduce activity and postpone grooming or play. If it lasts more than a day, or comes with not eating or other symptoms, contact the vet.
Skipping one meal is worth watching. Skipping two or more meals means contact the vet. Cats that stop eating for more than a day can develop serious liver problems, so call the vet sooner for cats.
